terms.gloss: a broad street; the main street of a town
evidence: Ter. Ad. 582: ad sinistram hāc rēctā platēā
Plaut. Cist. 534: quī rēctā platēā cursum hūc contendit suom
terms.comment: The broad street of a Greek or Roman town, as against its lanes (vīcī, angiporta); in the street scenes of comedy people come straight up the platēa. Latin has no set phrase for “the main street”. To single one out, call it the busiest: celeberrima is what the authors say of a much-frequented place (celeberrimō locō, Cic. Att. 12.23).

phrases.latin: sed quis hic est quī rēctā platēā cursum hūc contendit suom?
phrases.english: but who’s this running this way straight up the street?
he blocked up the gates and walled off the lanes and the main streets

phrases.latin: Haec via omnium celeberrima est; tenē manum meam.
phrases.english: This is the busiest street of all; hold my hand.

sources: Lewis & Short: platea · Lewis & Short: celeber
